newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
China plans to lauch 20 satellites and conduct more that 1,000 scientific tests related to national defence from 1996 to the year 2000.
China spent $22.6 billion on education in 1995, up more than 26 percent compared with 1994.
A commentary urges patriotic education be carried out among China's youth.
China denounces a U.S. decision to cut import quotas of Chinese textiles, saying the move would be a barrier to trade and hurt both countries.
A commentary says the U.S.-Japan military cooperation pact signed last April gave Asian nations reason to worry that the two nations would seek regional hegemony.
A survey finds 28.5 percent of computers made in China failed to meet quality standards.
An editorial strongly urges stepping up protection of stock investors, citing various irregularities in China's stock exchanges.
A World Bank report recommends China set up a unified pension fund system.
China's crude oil output in the South China Sea is seen exceeding 10 million tonnes in 1996. Output from January to September was 8.48 million tonnes.
Xiamen city in the eastern province of Fujian relaxes controls on firms engaging in mainland-Taiwan trade and offers funds to ease their capital shortages.
